request.text:
You are the vision observer for GeoKnow / ESOGU "foraminifera-fossil".
You are NOT a taxonomic authority and you do NOT replace the project's scoring engine.

Goal: look at the attached optical image(s) of a microfossil (thin section or reflected-light photomicrograph) and fill the project's character sheet CHR_01–CHR_21.

Hard rules
1. Observe first. Identify only as a tentative suggestion.
2. Never invent a character. If it is not clearly visible, use state NOT_OBSERVABLE. If visible but ambiguous, use UNCERTAIN.
3. NOT_OBSERVABLE is not ABSENT. Do not mark ABSENT unless the relevant area is exposed and the feature is clearly missing.
4. Keep CHR_05 and CHR_06 separate:
   - CHR_05 = serial arrangement only (UNISERIAL, BISERIAL, TRISERIAL, QUINQUELOCULINE, TRILOCULINE, BILOCULINE, ANNULAR, CYCLIC, IRREGULAR_SERIAL, OTHER)
   - CHR_06 = coiling (PLANISPIRAL, TROCHOSPIRAL, STREPTOSPIRAL, GLOMOSPIRAL, IRREGULAR_COILING, UNCOILED)
5. Do not force a species name. Prefer genus or morphogroup. If evidence is weak, identification_status = INDETERMINATE.
6. This tool is academic and non-commercial. Do not present the answer as an official Foraminifera.eu, WoRMS, or museum determination.
7. Reply with VALID JSON only. No markdown, no preamble, no trailing text.
8. Allowed observation states: PRESENT, ABSENT, NOT_OBSERVABLE, UNCERTAIN.
9. Allowed identification_status values: CONFIRMED_GENUS, PROBABLE_GENUS, CANDIDATE_GENUS, INDETERMINATE, NO_MATCH_WITHIN_CORE_TAXA.
10. If the object is not a foraminifer, set object_is_foraminifer=false and fill every CHR with NOT_OBSERVABLE / null.

Allowed values (use ONLY these codes)

CHR_01 Test composition: AGGLUTINATED | PORCELANEOUS | HYALINE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_02 Test shape: GLOBULAR | SAC_LIKE | TUBULAR | ELONGATE | FUSIFORM | OVOID | LENTICULAR | DISCOIDAL | FLATTENED | CONICAL | HIGH_CONICAL | FLABELLIFORM | STELLATE | IRREGULAR | OTHER | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_03 Septation: PRESENT | ABSENT | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_04 Chamber number organization: UNDIVIDED | MULTICHAMBERED | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_05 Chamber arrangement: UNISERIAL | BISERIAL | TRISERIAL | QUINQUELOCULINE | TRILOCULINE | BILOCULINE | ANNULAR | CYCLIC | IRREGULAR_SERIAL | OTHER | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_06 Coiling pattern: PLANISPIRAL | TROCHOSPIRAL | STREPTOSPIRAL | GLOMOSPIRAL | IRREGULAR_COILING | UNCOILED | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_07 Coiling plane: SINGLE_PLANE | CHANGING_PLANES | MULTIDIRECTIONAL | NOT_APPLICABLE | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_08 Involution/evolution: INVOLUTE | SEMI_INVOLUTE | EVOLUTE | NOT_APPLICABLE | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_09 Ontogenetic arrangement change: NONE | PLANISPIRAL_TO_UNISERIAL | PLANISPIRAL_TO_BISERIAL | BISERIAL_TO_UNISERIAL | TRISERIAL_TO_BISERIAL | TRISERIAL_TO_UNISERIAL | COILED_TO_SERIAL | OTHER | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_10 Internal complexity: SIMPLE | SUBDIVIDED | COMPLEX | RETICULATE | LABYRINTHIC | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_11 Secondary chamberlets: PRESENT | ABSENT | WEAKLY_DEVELOPED | WELL_DEVELOPED | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_12 Embryonic apparatus: SIMPLE | BILOCULAR | MULTILOCULAR | COMPLEX | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_13 Radial/internal partitions: ABSENT | RADIAL | VERTICAL | SUBEPIDERMAL | RETICULATE | OTHER | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_14 Pillars: PRESENT | ABSENT | WEAK | STRONG | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_15 Lateral chamberlets: PRESENT | ABSENT | WEAKLY_DEVELOPED | WELL_DEVELOPED | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_16 Aperture type: TERMINAL | INTERIOMARGINAL | BASAL | MULTIPLE | SLIT_LIKE | CRIBRATE | OTHER | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_17 Marginal cord: PRESENT | ABSENT | WEAK | STRONG | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_18 Septal filaments: ABSENT | SIMPLE | CURVED | WAVY | RETICULATE | COMPLEX | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_19 Attachment mode: FREE | ATTACHED | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_20 Dimorphism: PRESENT | ABSENT | MEGALOSPHERIC_FORM | MICROSPHERIC_FORM | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_21 Section orientation: AXIAL | EQUATORIAL | OBLIQUE | TANGENTIAL | UNKNOWN

Observation object format for every CHR:
{"value": "<CODE or null>", "state": "PRESENT|ABSENT|NOT_OBSERVABLE|UNCERTAIN", "reason": "one short sentence"}

When state is NOT_OBSERVABLE or UNCERTAIN, value may be null.
For CHR_01, if composition cannot be judged from lighting, value=UNCERTAIN and state=UNCERTAIN.
For CHR_21, state is usually PRESENT and value is the section type; use UNKNOWN if the view is external, not a thin section.

Context from the user:
- locality: unknown
- age / stratigraphy: unknown
- lighting / magnification: unknown
- scale: unknown
- views provided: unknown

    "CHR_01": {"value": "HYALINE", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Microcrystalline or radially fibrous calcareous wall structure typical of larger benthic foraminifers."},
    "CHR_02": {"value": "STELLATE", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "The test exhibits ray-like arms extending outward from a central region."},

    "CHR_05": {"value": "ANNULAR", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Chambers are arranged in concentric, annular rings around the center."},
    "CHR_06": {"value": "NOT_OBSERVABLE", "state": "NOT_OBSERVABLE", "reason": "Coiling in early stage is obscured by equatorial section view of advanced cyclic growth."},
    "CHR_07": {"value": "SINGLE_PLANE", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Equatorial slice showing a single plane of growth."},
    "CHR_08": {"value": "NOT_APPLICABLE", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Cyclic/annular arrangement makes involution/evolution categories inapplicable."},
    "CHR_09": {"value": "NOT_OBSERVABLE", "state": "NOT_OBSERVABLE", "reason": "Initial chambers in the very center are not clearly resolved at this magnification."},
    "CHR_10": {"value": "COMPLEX", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Presence of chamberlets and complex internal structures."},
    "CHR_11": {"value": "WELL_DEVELOPED", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Secondary chamberlets are clearly visible dividing the annular chambers."},
    "CHR_12": {"value": "SIMPLE", "state": "UNCERTAIN", "reason": "Central embryonic apparatus is faintly discernible but details are unclear."},
    "CHR_13": {"value": "RADIAL", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Radial partitions and stolons are visible along the stellar rays."},
    "CHR_14": {"value": "PRESENT", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Pillars or pillar-like structures are visible in the central area and rays."},
    "CHR_15": {"value": "NOT_OBSERVABLE", "state": "NOT_OBSERVABLE", "reason": "Lateral chamberlets cannot be clearly distinguished in this equatorial view."},
    "CHR_16": {"value": "MULTIPLE", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Apertural characteristics represented by multiple openings/stolons along the periphery."},
    "CHR_17": {"value": "ABSENT", "state": "ABSENT", "reason": "No distinct marginal cord like in Operculina or Nummulites."},
    "CHR_18": {"value": "ABSENT", "state": "ABSENT", "reason": "Septal filaments are not expressed in this internal equatorial view."},
    "CHR_19": {"value": "FREE", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "Morphology is symmetrical and discoidal-stellate, indicative of a free-living benthic form."},
    "CHR_20": {"value": "NOT_OBSERVABLE", "state": "NOT_OBSERVABLE", "reason": "Proloculus size variation cannot be determined from a single specimen."},
    "CHR_21": {"value": "EQUATORIAL", "state": "PRESENT", "reason": "The thin section cuts through the equatorial plane showing the cyclic chambers and rays."}

  "vlm_suggestion": {
    "identification_status": "CANDIDATE_GENUS",
    "best_open_id": "Asterigerinidae or Orbitoididae indet. (cf. Asterocyclina / Orbitoids)",

    "lookalikes": ["Orbitoides", "Discocyclina"],
    "why_not_species_level": "Species identification requires detailed axial sections, embryonic apparatus measurement, and stratigraphic context."

It features concentric annular chamber layers crossed by radial rays, characteristic of complex rotaliids or orbitoids. Key features include well-developed chamberlets, internal radial partitions, and a hyaline calcareous wall.",
  "student_explanation_tr": "Bu görüntü, yıldız biçimli (stellate) test yapısına sahip büyük bir bentik foraminiferin ekvatoral kesitini göstermektedir.     "Ekvatoral kesitin tam düzlemde olup olmadığı doğrulanmalı."
  ],
  "disclaimer_tr": "Bu bir öğretim ve karar-destek çıktısıdır; resmi taksonomik teşhis değildir."
}

CHR_01.reason: Microcrystalline or radially fibrous calcareous wall structure typical of larger benthic foraminifers.

CHR_02.reason: The test exhibits ray-like arms extending outward from a central region.

CHR_03.reason: Chambers are visibly divided by septa.

CHR_04.reason: Many chambers are clearly visible forming annular or cyclic layers with stellar rays.

CHR_05.reason: Chambers are arranged in concentric, annular rings around the center.

CHR_06.reason: Coiling in early stage is obscured by equatorial section view of advanced cyclic growth.

CHR_07.reason: Equatorial slice showing a single plane of growth.

CHR_08.reason: Cyclic/annular arrangement makes involution/evolution categories inapplicable.

CHR_09.reason: Initial chambers in the very center are not clearly resolved at this magnification.

CHR_10.reason: Presence of chamberlets and complex internal structures.

CHR_11.reason: Secondary chamberlets are clearly visible dividing the annular chambers.

CHR_12.reason: Central embryonic apparatus is faintly discernible but details are unclear.

CHR_13.reason: Radial partitions and stolons are visible along the stellar rays.

CHR_14.reason: Pillars or pillar-like structures are visible in the central area and rays.

CHR_15.reason: Lateral chamberlets cannot be clearly distinguished in this equatorial view.

CHR_16.reason: Apertural characteristics represented by multiple openings/stolons along the periphery.

CHR_17.reason: No distinct marginal cord like in Operculina or Nummulites.

CHR_18.reason: Septal filaments are not expressed in this internal equatorial view.

CHR_19.reason: Morphology is symmetrical and discoidal-stellate, indicative of a free-living benthic form.

CHR_20.reason: Proloculus size variation cannot be determined from a single specimen.

CHR_21.reason: The thin section cuts through the equatorial plane showing the cyclic chambers and rays.

vlm_suggestion.best_open_id: Asterigerinidae or Orbitoididae indet. (cf. Asterocyclina / Orbitoids)

candidate_genera.why: Stellate test with distinct rays and cyclic chamber arrangement in equatorial section.

candidate_genera.name: Discocyclina
candidate_genera.why: Similar annular chamber arrangement, but typically lacks prominent protruding rays.

vlm_suggestion.why_not_species_level: Species identification requires detailed axial sections, embryonic apparatus measurement, and stratigraphic context.

observation.student_explanation_en: This image shows an equatorial thin section of a larger benthic foraminifer with a stellate (star-like) shape. It features concentric annular chamber layers crossed by radial rays, characteristic of complex rotaliids or orbitoids. Key features include well-developed chamberlets, internal radial partitions, and a hyaline calcareous wall.
observation.student_explanation_tr: Bu görüntü, yıldız biçimli (stellate) test yapısına sahip büyük bir bentik foraminiferin ekvatoral kesitini göstermektedir. Konsantrik halkasal odacıklar ve bunları kesen ışınsal kollar, karmaşık yapılı bir formu işaret eder. Gelişmiş odacıkcıklar, iç bölmeler ve hiyalin kalsitik duvar en belirgin özellikleridir.
expert_checklist_tr: Merkezi embryonic yapının boyutları ve morfolojisi incelenmeli.
Işınsal kolların (rays) yapısı ve ara odacıkcık (chamberlet) düzeni kontrol edilmeli.
Ekvatoral kesitin tam düzlemde olup olmadığı doğrulanmalı.
observation.disclaimer_tr: Bu bir öğretim ve karar-destek çıktısıdır; resmi taksonomik teşhis değildir.
